architectural_layer: existing local PR identity owner, provider read adapter and submission/prospective consumers
operation_side: authenticated query before qualification or mutation
invariant: An authenticated bound PR supplies its exact base/head relationship; default branch is not a substitute for that relationship. Candidate-local proof never grants provider certification, protected-main or release authority.
contract: Extend the existing LocalPRContext owner rather than introduce a second base resolver, CLI intent flag or semantic registry. Preserve exact legacy local/non-provider unbound context serialization and existing public CLI grammar; newly authenticated GitHub absence additionally binds repository identity.

Distinguish repository default branch, PR base branch and exact comparison SHA, provider-observed head and current local candidate. Newly authored descendants are not silently identical to an already observed provider head.

Authenticate provider repository identity against the selected remote and complete open PR inventory; exactly one branch/repository match binds a PR. Duplicate, malformed, moved, wrong repository, wrong ref or unavailable bound facts reject before generation/proof/effects. Absence must be authenticated; provider errors never become an empty inventory.

Fetch and verify exact referenced Git objects and ancestry through the existing immutable Git read retry owner. Attempt count is bounded; complete operation/runtime deadline envelopes remain an explicit qualification requirement. Preserve default-branch behavior for authenticated unbound and genuinely local non-provider repositories; unprovable GitHub identity cannot confer submit authority.

Propagate the same comparison context to source checks, changelog, planning, local synthetic PR event, prospective proof, exact push, existing PR projection and late unchanged checks. A provider/local head advancement requires an explicit same-branch descendant transition and reauthentication at its consuming boundary.

Preserve separate authority contexts: a feature-branch PR base does not grant protected-default-main, bounded/phase, controller or release authority. Existing repository protection and finalizer/evaluator owners retain their propositions. No force-push, blind retry or mutation inference.

Existing PR reuse binds actual base ref/SHA rather than requiring every PR base equal repository default. Creation of an unbound PR continues to derive the default target. Protected merge requests remain independently gated by the actual target protection contract.

All existing concrete success/error serialization must remain compatible in unchanged unbound contexts. Changes to previously rejected or unprovable states are additive safety behavior; any unavoidable valid public contract break blocks activation pending explicit migration/version decision.
Remain isolated from live canonical attempt 5. Do not merge or activate an incomplete subset that changes local base while leaving consumers on default-branch assumptions.

Represent a bound nondefault PR as PR progress, never as the rendered future default-main bounded/phase proposition. Existing default-main graph projection remains unchanged. Derive this candidate projection from the authenticated comparison context, not caller intent.

Extend the existing protected_merge closed state population with nondefault_base: exact paired base/default refs bind its identity; action is observe_same_subject, successor pr_pending, release authority false. It grants no auto-merge or normal-merge mutation. Existing default-target behavior and legacy evidence readability remain unchanged.

When base/default refs are present, mutation-bearing protected_merge states require equality; nondefault_base requires inequality and both refs. Missing/partial/wrong context rejects. Canonical submit supplies these facts and never invokes protected mutation adapters for the nondefault target. A stacked PR can still publish exact candidate progress and require independent provider PR proof.

Installed controller/evaluator and source protection owners remain independent. No feature-branch base can replace protected default-main policy or confer lifecycle/release authority. Full consumer controls must prove this before integration.

Before integration, satisfy the explicit protected-default/evaluator source separation matrix in audits/issue-394/bound-pr-authority-context-research.json. Existing default-base guards cannot be removed without equivalent independent source qualification; preserve #425 regressions and immutable v2.3.4.

Consume new bound context metadata atomically before provider retry reads: exact repository/ID, PR number/node and complete base/provider-head binding must agree with the independently proved PR projection; malformed or partial binding rejects without normalization, read or mutation. Legacy unbound context remains readable.

Direct protection prospective admission must pass its supplied authenticated read API unchanged to the existing comparison context owner. No implicit environment-client substitution; provider errors preserve cause and stop before protection validation.

Capture protected-default commit/tree independently of comparison base for authenticated GitHub contexts. Require provider exact refs/heads/default commit agreement with the fetched immutable Git object before and after bound/absence discovery; malformed, moved or wrong-type refs reject. Preserve five-field genuinely local legacy serialization. These observations alone confer no policy/evaluator authority; downstream separation and movement controls remain required.

Existing prospective policy owner must receive the complete authenticated context, bind source policy to its independently observed protected-default commit/tree, and reconstruct policy-affecting paths relative to that source. Product comparison paths remain unchanged. Reject partial snapshots, wrong subjects and unavailable/mismatched protected objects; feature-base policy changes cannot disappear from invalidation closure. Legacy genuinely local/default contexts retain prior behavior.
